newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania eyes CEFTA, signs Slovenia trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania eyes CEFTA, signs Slovenia trade deal.

text.p: Lithuania and Slovenia on Friday signed a free trade deal, another step on the Baltic state's path to membership of the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA).

Lithuania has set its sights on CEFTA membership but is also aiming to enter the European Union (EU). CEFTA groups Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and Slovenia and Lithuania now has free trade deals with all except Hungary.
"Barriers will fall significantly on January 1," Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun told a news conference. But he said tariffs on some goods would remain for two to three years.
The agreement with Slovenia is expected to boost trade between the two countries, which rose from $6.0 million in 1994 to $9.0 million in 1995.
Kracun said Lithuania may be able to join CEFTA next year, when Slovenia chairs the organisation's presidency.
Lithuanian Foreign Minister Povilas Gylys said that his country hoped to seal a free trade with Hungary by February 1997. -- Riga Newsroom +371 7 22 66 93
